report.summary: During the requested investigation window, checkout-service resident memory rose 1.8x, from 677.75MiB to 1220.35MiB. Logs also show high Java heap pressure and Java heap space out-of-memory errors, supporting heap exhaustion as the leading hypothesis. The evidence does not identify why heap usage grew.

likely_causes.title: Java heap exhaustion, potentially from excessive retained or allocated heap objects
likely_causes.rationale: The rising resident memory coincides with warnings of 92% heap usage and GC overhead approaching, followed by explicit Java heap space errors. This supports heap exhaustion, but does not establish a leak, specific code path, or deployment regression.

supporting_evidence.detail: Threshold-validated resident memory rose 1.8x, from 677.75MiB to 1220.35MiB; anomaly_detected=True.
17 WARN samples reported “GC overhead limit approaching; heap usage 92%” between 2026-10-26T11:48:32+00:00 and 2026-10-26T13:04:32+00:00.
5 ERROR samples reported “java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space” between 2026-10-26T12:42:32+00:00 and 2026-10-26T13:04:32+00:00.

next_steps: Inspect heap dumps or allocation and retention profiles from affected instances to identify what occupies the heap.
Review garbage-collection metrics and configured heap limits alongside resident-memory measurements.
Check deployment and configuration changes during the investigation window; log samples identify version v1.4.2 but do not establish when it was deployed.
Verify request-rate trends before considering traffic growth as a contributor.
Reconcile the message query that returned zero OutOfMemoryError matches with the ERROR query that returned five Java heap out-of-memory samples.
